key_insight: Increasing the O₂/C₂H₂ ratio improved coating density, smoothness, and adhesion, while peak microhardness occurred at a ratio of 1.1.
engineering_relevance: Gas-ratio control offers a practical way to tailor flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings on AISI 321 steel to different property priorities.
method: Deposited coatings using a Metal Coat 6PM-II flame-spray system at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2.
Monitored spraying conditions with an Accuraspray 4.0 diagnostic system.
Characterized microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: From ratio 1.0 to 1.2, porosity decreased from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness fell from 4.70 ± 0.09 to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and adhesion rose from 22.14 ± 4.3 to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa; peak average microhardness was 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The abstract reports only three gas ratios and no service-life testing, so long-term performance and transferability to other spray setups remain unverified.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
